name: PLS Launcher
tagline: One tap opens the whole Pulse family, full screen.
overview: PLS Launcher is a small Android app you tap like any other. It opens a field that fills the whole screen with every Pulse Labs app: the ones you have are lit and open with one tap, the ones you don't have yet show as faded ghosts with their names. Arrange them in layers of your own: hold an app to move it, resize a layer, hide what you don't want, add any other app from the device, and undo any step. It has no internet permission; it only looks at which apps are on the device.

capabilities.title: One tap, the whole family
capabilities.text: Tap PLS Launcher and a field fills the whole screen, edge to edge, with a red border that follows the screen's own rounded corners. Every Pulse Labs app is in it.

proofs.caption: The field on the opened Fold: 3 of 9 Pulse apps on this device

capabilities.title: Apps you have are lit and open with one tap
capabilities.text: Pulse apps on the device show their real icon. One tap opens the app.

proofs.caption: Tap Keyboard Studio: it opens

capabilities.title: Apps you don't have yet are ghosts
capabilities.text: Pulse apps you don't have show as a dashed outline with a faded line icon and their name, marked Not installed. Tapping one does nothing.

proofs.caption: After tapping the PLS PDF ghost: nothing opened, still on the launcher

capabilities.title: New Pulse apps appear by themselves
capabilities.text: Any Pulse Labs app on the device shows up lit, even one that isn't on the built-in list yet.

proofs.caption: PLS Clock HUD isn't on the built-in list but shows up lit (9 apps counted)

capabilities.title: A ghost lights up once installed
capabilities.text: Install a Pulse app and its ghost turns into a lit tile the next time you open the launcher.

capabilities.title: Layers that fill themselves
capabilities.text: The launcher starts with two layers that fill themselves: Your Pulse apps and More from Pulse Labs, each with its count.

proofs.caption: Your Pulse apps (3) and More from Pulse Labs (6)

capabilities.title: Add your own layers
capabilities.text: Make a named layer (Work, Daily, Games...). New layers go on top and show a Drop apps here box until you fill them.

proofs.caption: Add a layer: type its name
New layer Daily, with its empty Drop apps here box

capabilities.title: Rename, reorder or remove a layer
capabilities.text: Each layer you made can be renamed, moved up or down, or removed. Removing a layer uninstalls nothing.

proofs.caption: Edit layer: name, Move up, Move down, Remove

capabilities.title: Hold any app to arrange
capabilities.text: Hold any app, lit or ghost, to jump into Arrange with that app picked: teal frame, an amber MOVE circle and a red minus.

proofs.caption: Held PLS Authenticator: picked, with MOVE and the red minus

capabilities.title: Drag to move
capabilities.text: Drag the MOVE circle to put the app anywhere: before or after another app, or into another layer.

proofs.caption: Dragged PLS Authenticator after PLS Clock HUD
Dragged Keyboard Studio into the Daily layer

capabilities.title: Tap for RESIZE, drag for size
capabilities.text: Tap the MOVE circle and it turns into a blue RESIZE circle. Drag right for bigger apps, left for smaller, live, for the whole layer.

proofs.caption: RESIZE mode at 100%
Dragged right: the layer at 157%

capabilities.title: Hide an app, and bring it back
capabilities.text: The red minus or HIDE takes an app off the launcher without uninstalling it. Hidden apps lists them; one tap shows one again.

proofs.caption: PLS Authenticator hidden: the layer now shows 2
Hidden apps: tap one to show it again
Shown again: nothing is hidden

capabilities.title: Each app's own options
capabilities.text: Tap a picked app again for its options: open it, choose its layer, move it earlier or later, or hide it.

proofs.caption: Keyboard Studio's options: layer, order, hide

capabilities.title: Add any app from this device
capabilities.text: Any app on the device can sit in the launcher too, in any layer.

proofs.caption: Add an app: the device's apps
The device's Clock app added to Daily

capabilities.title: Undo step by step, or Cancel it all
capabilities.text: The red arrow takes back one change per tap. Cancel takes back every change in this Arrange session. The green check keeps them.

proofs.caption: One tap on the red arrow: the size is back to 100%
Before Cancel: an app was just hidden (Hidden apps (1))
After Cancel: the hidden app is back

capabilities.title: Put everything back
capabilities.text: One button returns the starting layout: your layers, hidden apps and added apps go away. Nothing is uninstalled, and it can be undone.

proofs.caption: Put everything back? It asks first
Back to the two starting layers
Red arrow: the Daily layer is back

capabilities.title: Your layout stays
capabilities.text: Layers, order, hidden and added apps are saved on the device and come back after the app is closed and opened again.

proofs.caption: After closing and reopening the app: Daily, Clock and the new order are still there

capabilities.title: Pulse dark, Light, or follow the phone
capabilities.text: Choose the look on first start; flip it any time with the eye button at the top.

proofs.caption: First start: choose your look
Light, picked on the first screen
Eye button: the launcher in Light

capabilities.title: Text size, font and app tile size
capabilities.text: Display settings: four text sizes, the Pulse font or the device's font, and Small, Medium or Large app tiles.

proofs.caption: Display: look, text size, font
App tile size: Large picked
The launcher with Large tiles

capabilities.title: Turn ghosts off
capabilities.text: A switch in Settings hides the apps you don't have, so only your own apps show.

proofs.caption: Settings: Show apps you don't have, turned off
The launcher with ghosts off

capabilities.title: Folded or open
capabilities.text: The field fits the screen it is on: two columns on the folded cover screen, five on the opened Fold.

proofs.caption: Folded cover screen (1080x2520)
Opened Fold

capabilities.title: How to use it, with Show me
capabilities.text: A manual explains every part, with Show me buttons that take you to the real screen.

proofs.caption: The manual
Show me under Faded apps opens Settings, where the ghost switch is

capabilities.title: Report a problem, your way
capabilities.text: Write what happened; your own email app opens addressed to support, and you review it before sending.

proofs.caption: Report a Problem, filled in with demo text
Your report is ready: review it in your email app

capabilities.title: Crash log kept on the device
capabilities.text: Crashes are kept on the device and only sent if you add them to a report.

proofs.caption: Crash log: no crashes recorded

capabilities.title: Offline by design
capabilities.text: No internet permission. It only looks at which apps are on this device, and that never leaves it.

proofs.caption: About: version 0.3.0, offline by design

demo.caption: 35 seconds on the test bench (opened Fold): choose a look, open the field, tap a ghost (nothing opens), hold an app to arrange it, drag it to a new place, switch to RESIZE and make the layer bigger, undo both steps, keep.

note: Captured on the Pulse test bench (Android 15 emulator, Fold profile) with demo data only.
